summary: Specifies a sockets API for advanced IPv6 applications, as a supplement to the basic API in RFC 3493. It targets programs such as ping, traceroute, and routing daemons that need raw sockets and access to IPv6 and ICMPv6 header fields. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Most programs just ask the network to deliver data. A few special tools need to look at the envelope and the labels. This memo gives programmers the tools for that in IPv6.

questions: how do i set ipv6 path mtu discovery
subtitle: The portable C sockets interface for programs that need raw IPv6 access, packet details, extension headers and path MTU control.

tldr.problem: Tools such as ping, traceroute and routing daemons need raw sockets and access to IPv6 header details. With IPv4 they were portable because most systems shared Berkeley code, but IPv6 has no common code base, so implementations could diverge.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines header structures and constants, raw socket rules (the kernel handles the ICMPv6 checksum, with an ICMPv6 type filter), and socket options and ancillary data for interface, addresses, hop limit, traffic class, extension headers and path MTU. It adds helper functions for building and parsing options.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational document that obsoletes RFC 2292 and says it may later be formally standardized by a more appropriate body.

today: RFC 3542 is an Informational document that obsoletes RFC 2292. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why an Advanced IPv6 Sockets API
sections.content:
RFC 3493 covers the basic IPv6 changes to the sockets API, for TCP and UDP applications. This document defines the advanced features, supplementing it for programs such as Ping, Traceroute and routing daemons, which typically use raw sockets to reach IPv6 or ICMPv6 header fields.

The motivation is portability. IPv4 raw socket programs compile on many hosts mainly because most IPv4 implementations started from the Berkeley source code or header files. IPv6 has no such common base, so the possibility of divergence is high and some standardization is needed.

The document also covers features that RFC 3493 leaves out: sending and receiving Routing headers, Hop-by-Hop options and Destination options, choosing the outgoing interface, learning the receiving interface, and path MTU control. It does not cover the authentication header or the encapsulating security payload header. It replaces RFC 2292 and, being Informational, notes that it may later be formally standardized by a more appropriate body.
sections.eli5: When every computer builds its own tools in a different way, a program written for one will not work on another. This memo is the shared instruction sheet so the special tools work everywhere.

sections.title: Common Header Structures and Constants
sections.content:
Advanced programs examine IPv6 and ICMPv6 header fields, so the RFC defines common C definitions in two new header files, <netinet/ip6.h> and <netinet/icmp6.h>. Fields are left in network byte order.

The ip6_hdr structure covers the IPv6 header. Constants give the Next Header values, such as IPPROTO_ROUTING (43), IPPROTO_FRAGMENT (44) and IPPROTO_ICMPV6 (58), and structures describe the Hop-by-Hop, Destination, Routing and Fragment headers. The icmp6_hdr structure comes with ICMPv6 type and code constants such as ICMP6_DST_UNREACH (1) and ICMP6_ECHO_REQUEST (128), plus definitions for Neighbor Discovery, Multicast Listener Discovery and Router Renumbering.

The RFC also adds an address comparison macro, IN6_ARE_ADDR_EQUAL, and names for the new protocols in /etc/protocols, so that getprotobyname() works portably.
sections.eli5: Before anyone can read the labels on an envelope, everyone has to agree on the names of the boxes on the label. This part gives every box an agreed name.

sections.title: IPv6 Raw Sockets
sections.content:
Raw sockets bypass the transport layer. With IPv6 they are used for ICMPv6 and for datagrams whose Next Header value the kernel does not process, such as OSPF for IPv6 and RSVP. All data on a raw socket is in network byte order. Unlike IPv4 raw sockets, complete packets with extension headers cannot be sent or received this way; ancillary data carries the extension headers and hop limit instead, so there is no equivalent of the IPv4 IP_HDRINCL option. On output the kernel fragments packets larger than the path MTU, and on input it reassembles them.

For an ICMPv6 raw socket the kernel always calculates and inserts the mandatory checksum. For other raw IPv6 sockets, the application sets the IPV6_CHECKSUM socket option with an offset, and the kernel then computes the checksum (including the IPv6 pseudo-header) on output and verifies it on input. It is disabled by default, and a positive odd offset is invalid.

An ICMPv6 raw socket can receive many more message types than an ICMPv4 one, so a per-socket filter selects types, using ICMP6_FILTER and six macros such as ICMP6_FILTER_SETBLOCKALL and ICMP6_FILTER_SETPASS. By default all types pass. The stack verifies the ICMPv6 checksum and should pass unknown types to applications for extensibility.
sections.eli5: A raw socket lets a program handle the network message directly. The system still does the boring math check for you, and you can tell it to hide the kinds of messages you do not care about.

sections.title: Packet Information and Extension Headers
sections.content:
The core of the API is a set of values an application can send or receive alongside data: the interface and source or destination address, the hop limit, the next hop, the traffic class, and the Routing, Hop-by-Hop and Destination options headers. They travel as ancillary data with sendmsg() and recvmsg(), or as sticky options set with setsockopt() that apply to every packet until changed. An ancillary item overrides the sticky option of the same name for that packet only.

To receive any of this information on a UDP or raw socket, the application enables a flag such as IPV6_RECVPKTINFO, IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT, IPV6_RECVRTHDR, IPV6_RECVHOPOPTS, IPV6_RECVDSTOPTS or IPV6_RECVTCLASS. TCP is deliberately left out, because TCP segments do not map one-to-one onto send and receive calls.

The in6_pktinfo structure carries an address and an interface index, so a UDP server can reply from the address and out the interface the request used. The outgoing interface follows a fixed order: an IPV6_PKTINFO ancillary item, then the sticky IPV6_PKTINFO, then IPV6_MULTICAST_IF for multicast, then the next hop. Hop limit and traffic class accept -1 for the kernel default, or 0 to 255. IPV6_NEXTHOP is a privileged option.

Extension headers are built and read through helper functions rather than raw bytes. Six inet6_rth_* functions build and examine a Routing header (Type 0 supports up to 127 intermediate nodes), and seven inet6_opt_* functions handle Hop-by-Hop and Destination options. Received headers are returned in the order they appeared in the packet.
sections.eli5: It is like sticking notes on the outside of an envelope: which door to leave by, how far it may travel, how important it is. You can put a note on one letter, or leave a standing note that goes on every letter.

sections.title: Path MTU and the r Commands
sections.content:
Unicast applications should usually let the kernel do path MTU discovery. The IPV6_USE_MIN_MTU option controls this: -1 (the default) discovers the path MTU for unicast but sends multicast at the minimum MTU, 0 always discovers it, and 1 always sends at the minimum MTU. The RFC notes that careless large multicast packets in IPv4 have caused an implosion of ICMPv4 error messages.

IPV6_DONTFRAG turns off the automatic insertion of a fragment header on UDP and raw sockets, which suits a tool like traceroute that wants to find the real path MTU. It is disabled by default. With IPV6_RECVPATHMTU, an application receives an IPV6_PATHMTU ancillary item, carrying an ip6_mtuinfo structure, when a packet is too big. On a connected socket, the IPV6_PATHMTU socket option reads the current value.

Finally, section 14 defines rresvport_af(), rcmd_af() and rexec_af(), address-family-aware versions of the library functions behind the "r" commands such as rlogin. They keep older applications working while allowing AF_INET6 sockets.
sections.eli5: Roads have a widest truck that fits. These options let a program ask how wide the road is, or just use a small truck that always fits.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The section is short. Setting certain Hop-by-Hop and Destination options may be restricted to privileged processes, and some of them may not be returned to non-privileged applications. The ability to specify an arbitrary source address using IPV6_PKTINFO must be prevented, at least for non-privileged processes.
sections.eli5: Not every program should be allowed to write any return address on a letter, since that would let it pretend to be someone else.
